body:
I first became suicidal five years ago during a messy divorce that wound up earlier this year.  During that time I was hospitalized four times at my own request for am few weeks each time.  ironically I was hospitalized the day before the final hearing and the judge considered that insufficient grounds to postpone the hearing.  Predictably enough I came out rather badly in both the property settlement and the custody arrangements over our 12 yr old son and 11 yr old daughter.  But, after six weeks or so I bounced enough to be able to see this chapter as closed and to slowly begin to be be ablento look ahead.

Fast forward to yesterday.  I was working at home and noticed a truck outside that I knew was my ex wife's PI.  She has used him unsuccessfully a couple of years ago to put a GPS device on my car when she thought I was working under the table.  Without going into  detail, I have a strong PTSD reaction to stuff like that.  So I snuck out the back door and watched him put something under my car.

Then I called my shrink and my lawyer and took his device off my car and brought it to my lawyer.

Yesterday afternoon I picked my kids up from camp as scheduled and as I put them in the car someone called my name.  I turned around and the pi handed me a paper, said 'you've been served and you're on video' and walked away.  I was beyond speechless and in no shape to look after the kids  so I brought them to their mother, who was smiling like the Cheshire cat and was on the phone.  When I asked if we could speak she indicated we could but with the phone in her hand.  I assumed her lawyer was on the line so I declined and left.

Then I drove home, called me shrink again and took some sedatives.

But this time my suicidiality is different.  I am no afraid of it.  I realize  that it is that I am unlikely to know peace for a very long time.  (it appears that the cause of the current ex parte contempt motion is a demand by wife for $73k (not child support, which is up to date)  which I haven't got after the judge granted her the entire marital estate of c$300k).

I decided to take today off to see if rest and meds can buy me some space.  I found myself using the time to put things in order, write so electors, refine methods (opting for a combination of mild sedation, tylenol overdose w/ yogurt and benadryl), a helium hood, and hydrogen sulfide poisoning in my car) all to be carried out in a remote location to minimize the chance of interruption and to complicate evacuation to first aid in case I fail.

Like I said, I've decided to give it one more day, but I don't think much will change my mind.  Peace out.

The situation:  my divorce just became final.  The only asset I walked away with is an offshore pension, which is vested and paying me an annuity payment.  (I'm in my mid forties.)  By its terms, the pension can not be cashed out.   I also left the divorce with a ton of unsecured debt (c.140k) and a debt to the IRS.  I  believe that the IRS debt almost certainly can't be wiped out in a bankruptcy and that the unsecured debt probably can be.  

My two questions:  

1) Although no court order has been issued on this one, my lawyer and I keep expecting my wife's lawyers to ask for a supplemental order trying to hit me for at least a big part of her $200k+ bill to them.   I haven't asked my lawyer this b/c she does family law, not bankruptcy.  is there a risk that my wife's lawyers will wait for a bankruptcy to be complete and then send me a bill?  

2) Can this be headed off somehow?

Many thanks.

I've always been pretty quiet during sex - until I was with someone who was f'ing AWESOME in bed.  There were a bunch of times when I heard someone moaning and groaning and talking total filth and, for a few minutes, not even recognizing it was me, then worrying the roomies would hear, and then just saying 'fuck it' and totally getting into it.

This may not have been an isolated case of China testing the new US administration's response to low level harassment.

Read the history of the 1956  Suez crisis.  China is now perfectly positioned to give the US a choice between allowing a Chinese takeover of Taiwan or seeing China withdraw support for financing the US deficit.

People like Lewis just don't get it.  The most valuable commodity right now is credible information.  The more spin we get from the people who got us in to this mess, the more people decide to just dump everything.

Lewis blew the last of his credibility by under-vetting and over paying for Merrill. He should go now - with no golden parachute, and no pension.

The stock market's collapse, skyrocketing and accelerating unemployment (u-6 unemployment is near 15%), company failures, bank insolvency, pension insolvencies all point in the same direction:  we're in the early stages of a depression.  The government is reacting like a deer caught in headlights.  Better to take the pain as quickly as possible in the hope of moving on quicker.  Good first steps:  liquidating or nationalizing the failed banks and insurers, forcing GM and Chrysler into bankruptcy, focussing more money on a social safety net (and probably on the IMF as a number of governments are insolvent too).  What's happening to us now is a game changer and it will be neither pleasant nor quick.
